questions.q: What does the Slack Spoke actually bundle?
options: Multiple independently-usable Connector Actions, such as Post Message, Create Channel, and Invite User
Only authentication configuration, with no actions at all
A copy of Slack's own admin console inside ServiceNow
A single monolithic action that does everything Slack can do at once
questions.explain: A Spoke bundles several separate, individually usable Connector Actions, each wrapping one specific operation.

questions.q: A flow that only needs to post a Slack notification — which Connector Action would it use?
options: The MID Server's Slack integration
All three bundled actions, every time, regardless of need
A generic REST step instead of any Spoke action
Post Message, without touching Create Channel or Invite User
questions.explain: Each Connector Action is independently usable — a flow only wires in the specific action it needs.

questions.q: How is a Connector Action modeled, compared to any other Flow Designer action from course 4?
options: Completely differently — it has no Inputs or Outputs at all
It only accepts raw JSON with no defined structure
The same way — it declares named Inputs the flow builder wires in and named Outputs it returns
It requires a Script step to be wired in manually
questions.explain: Connector Actions share the same Inputs/Outputs action model as any other Flow Designer step.

questions.q: What does a Connector Action like Post Message hide from the flow builder?
options: The name of the action itself
Nothing — the flow builder must configure the raw API call manually
The channel name input field
Authentication against the external system and the request/response formatting its API requires
questions.explain: The Spoke handles authentication (via an Authentication Profile) and API-specific formatting internally, so the flow builder never has to.

questions.q: As an admin or developer working with a Spoke, what is your responsibility beyond what a flow builder does?
options: Nothing — Spokes require no setup at all
Avoiding Authentication Profiles entirely when using a Spoke
Confirming the Spoke is licensed and installed, connecting its Authentication Profile, and choosing which bundled actions a flow needs
Rewriting the Spoke's internal REST calls from scratch for every flow
questions.explain: The admin/developer handles licensing, authentication setup, and selecting the right bundled action — groundwork the flow builder shouldn't need to think about.
